title: Context compaction without losing the thread
excerpt: Long agent sessions die in two ways: the context window fills up, or you summarize so hard the model forgets the constraint that mattered. Here is how I compact history without inventing a new conversation.
content:
Every multi-turn agent hits the same wall: the transcript gets long, the window gets tight, and someone suggests "just summarize." Summarize wrong and you delete the only sentence that said *never* refund without a ticket ID.

I treat compaction as a **lossy compression step with a non-negotiable retain list** — not a vibe-based rewrite of the chat.

---

## What must survive every compact

Before any summarizer runs, I pin these into a structured state object the model always sees:

- User goal + success criteria
- Hard constraints / policy (refund rules, PII rules, tool deny list)
- Open todos and decisions already made
- Tool facts with IDs (ticket `T-1842`, order `ORD-9…`) — not paraphrases
- Failure modes already tried (so the agent stops looping)

Everything else — witty asides, failed search queries, raw tool dumps — is fair game to drop or compress.

---

## Three layers, not one giant summary

1. **Working state** — JSON the app owns: goal, constraints, entities, step budget left.
2. **Rolling summary** — 1–2 paragraphs of narrative for human-readable continuity.
3. **Recent raw turns** — last N messages + last tool results, full fidelity.

The model gets all three. The summarizer only rewrites layer 2. Layer 1 is updated by code from tool results, not by the LLM "remembering."

---

## When to compact

Triggers that work better than "every 10 turns":

- Token budget crosses ~60–70% of the model window
- After a successful tool batch (facts landed in state)
- Before a handoff to another agent or model tier
- When the same tool query repeats twice (thrash → compact + replan)

Do not compact mid-tool-call. Finish the step, persist facts, then compress.

---

## Eval the summarizer like a feature

I keep a small suite of sessions where a constraint appears early and a violation is attempted late. Compaction fails if the model complies with the bad request after summarize.

Also track:

- Constraint retention rate post-compact
- Entity ID accuracy (hallucinated ticket numbers = fail)
- Steps-to-resolution before vs after compaction
- Cost and latency of the compact call itself

If compaction saves tokens but raises wrong-action rate, you did not save money — you bought quieter incidents.

---

## Security note

Summaries are still model output. Do not let a compact step rewrite system policy. Keep policy in app-owned state. Redact PII before the summarizer if that text should never live in provider logs.

---

## Ship checklist

- [ ] App-owned state for goals, constraints, entity IDs
- [ ] Summarizer only touches the narrative layer
- [ ] Recent raw window kept for local grounding
- [ ] Eval cases that hide a constraint early and test it late
- [ ] Logs: pre/post token counts, compact reason, retention check result

Compaction is memory hygiene. Done well, the agent stays cheap and still knows what it promised not to do.
